societies.name: Men's Rugby
societies.standing_terms: Rugby at the Rec in October is the main fixture. Befriend the chair — it buys you practice filming at ordinary matches, and you can hand them the footage afterwards.
societies.cautions: They have done a serious sit-down format for Movember before. Do not repeat it. They are up for anything that raises money.

societies.name: SU Sport (general)
societies.standing_terms: Liaise through the SU sport leads and the media exec. One named person on your team owns all comms with the SU and the rugby chair.
societies.cautions: Do not oversell a livestream while the team is still finding its feet — falling short after charging leaves them disgruntled.
societies.charge_policy: Generally free. Charge for big ticketed events they are earning from, e.g. kickboxing.

societies.name: Dance Soc
societies.standing_terms: Camera at the back of the theatre with a mic picking up the room — they want to hear the tap noises. Ask them to book the middle seats on the back row so you can set up there.
societies.cautions: NEVER take the sound desk feed. This was done once and it was wrong. Camera can be left static, recording, and collected afterwards.

societies.name: BUST / BUSMS
societies.standing_terms: BUST have their own camera now. BUSMS bring someone who makes DVDs from the footage. If they do ask, establish whether they want audience audio (mic on a camera at the back) or the sound desk feed — for BUST specifically.

societies.name: Backstage
societies.standing_terms: Freshers week and Summer Ball only. They charge for SDI reels — buy and mark up our own so the charge goes away.
societies.cautions: Log every item you let them rig so no cable or kit leaves with them. Cameras get set up with you present. They do not switch cameras or touch our kit during arena nights. Make sure the women on the team are respected and know to tell you if something is off.
societies.charge_policy: They charge us. Not the other way round.

events.title: A-level results day post
events.brief: Congratulate students and say we look forward to meeting them. Promo and tradition — Section Ia.

prep.label: Draft copy + graphic

events.title: Media Hub set up and functional
events.brief: Section Ia, in bold: the hub has to be functional AHEAD of freshers week. Studio, editing area, gallery, storage.

prep.label: New Google Drive folder for the year
Everyone added to the Drive as contributor
prep.detail: Ela needs manager so she can make marketing folders.

prep.label: Enough SD cards in stock
SU leadership + finance training done

events.title: Committee meeting — freshers plan
events.brief: Section Ia — get to know each other, then delegate freshers coverage: who is doing what, and when they are back in Bath.

prep.label: Meet the committee post goes up

events.title: Welcome Weekend — Night 1
events.brief: Interviews with freshers from 22:30 for an hour or two, until enough usable content is gathered. Lighthearted questions, nothing that insults the SU or promotes anything illegal. Clips out the next day, 3 min max, swearing cut.

events.title: Welcome Weekend — Night 2
events.brief: Campus night. Two teams with kit, or alternate campus and town across the weekend.

events.title: Freshers Fair — stall
events.brief: Sweets to draw people in, plus TV trivia for prizes: easy / medium / hard = 1 / 2 / 3 sweets. Categories the Office, Gossip Girl, Doctor Who — keep it on the TV theme so it does not overlap with Filmsoc. Three QR codes on the table.

events.title: Sports Fair — stall
events.brief: Section Ib, in bold: be at the sports fair to advertise livestreaming and sports coverage. Roving pair asking clubs 'did you know CampusTV can livestream your matches?'

events.title: Arena Night 1
events.brief: Interviews outside from 22:00 — new questions and a new interviewer each night so it does not look like the same two people. Vision mix and PTZ 22:00 till 02:00. SD card into the ATEM and record pressed. Upload from the hub PC at 02:00 so it is on the Drive to edit tomorrow.

prep.label: SD card into the ATEM, record pressed
Rig with Backstage — log every item they touch
Arena-night graphics from Helen
prep.detail: See the 2024 freshers week folder for last year's.

events.title: Camera training — new members
events.brief: The week after freshers, while the interest is still fresh. Membership required to attend — check the SU list. 2–3 of the team confident enough to assist and answer questions.

prep.label: Cross-check attendee memberships on the SU site

events.title: Editing training — DaVinci
events.brief: DaVinci because it is free. Members can equally learn at home on Drive material — but they must not have delete access to the footage.

events.title: Rugby at the Rec
events.brief: Arrive three hours before, and before gates open, so everyone knows their role and everything is set up. Three cameras minimum: gantry (roof), SU box, and one roaming which doubles for interviews. B-roll for the highlights video. De-rig kit can go home with someone, but travel back to campus together and check everything you brought is back.

prep.label: Bus / driver sorted for kit to the venue
Count kit back in at campus, not at the venue

events.title: SU Instagram takeover
events.brief: Section IVb — organise far in advance of a big event and post the day across their stories. Speak to Helen a few weeks ahead. Pinned to Rugby at the Rec.

prep.label: Agree the date with Helen

events.title: Alumni fund — window 1
events.brief: Section IIId — opens around October/November, and again in January. The later you apply the later the money arrives. Look through Peter's previous applications. Portray a need and how it benefits the group.

prep.label: Confirm the exact dates with Helen and Angus
Read Peter's previous applications

events.title: Movember with Men's Rugby
events.brief: They are always up for raising money. Do NOT repeat the serious sit-down format — they have done it before.

events.title: National Television Day
events.brief: Section If, in full: 'Please do something its on the 21st of November.' Nothing planned yet.

events.title: NaSTA BBC trip — London
events.brief: Section VId — keep your eyes peeled on the NaSTA group chats, they run BBC trips in November. Advertise to the general chat and organise group travel by train.

events.title: Snowball
events.brief: Section Ie — B-roll for a montage. Interviews optional, the team decides.

events.title: Alumni fund — window 2
events.brief: The January opening. Caela's view: unlikely to land two years running, but worth the application.

events.title: NaSTA membership fee due
events.brief: Section VIa — an email lands in the ctvmanager account. Speak to the NaSTA Instagram or Helen if the payment gives trouble.

events.title: Masquerade Ball
events.brief: Section Ie — B-roll for a montage, interviews at the team's discretion.

events.title: Dance Soc showcase
events.brief: Static camera on the back row, middle seats, with a mic picking up the room. Set it recording, leave, come back for it.

events.title: Varsity — Cardiff Met
events.brief: Section Ig — set up a team, plan whether you are going, discuss plans with Cardiff Met. Caela's view: B-roll only, because the SU will not allow kit to travel that far.

events.title: NaSTA submissions close
events.brief: Section VIe — read the export settings carefully and look up how to meet them. Getting this wrong costs awards and invalidates submissions. Submit for as many categories as possible.

events.title: NaSTA Awards
events.brief: Section VIf/VIg — advertise hard, it is not fun when nobody goes. Travel together, share an Airbnb, count everyone in and out. Nominations are announced beforehand but there are unannounced categories, so go regardless.

Group travel + accommodation booked
Ask the exec what can be subsidised

events.title: Summer Ball
events.brief: Section Ih — like a freshers arena night but one night, plus B-roll of the fair ground. SORT YOUR OWN TEAM'S ACCREDITATION.

events.title: Handover — next station manager
events.brief: Section VII, Caela's closing note: securing a station manager for next year is the priority that keeps CTV alive. CTV OS exports the document.

Export the playbook as next year's handover

tasks.title: Get Helen to give you access to the ctvmanager mailbox
tasks.detail: Log in to your own Outlook account, then open the other mailbox from there.

tasks.title: Log into Instagram and YouTube and review the last few years
tasks.detail: Caela will pass you the passwords. The whole committee needs Instagram access so they can post. Delete nothing from previous years — cover images are fine for neatening the feed.

tasks.title: Make this year's Google Drive folder
tasks.detail: Copy the structure of the last few years. Change the folder text colour on your laptop so you do not confuse it with last year's.

tasks.title: Complete the SU leadership training
tasks.detail: Dull, mandatory, and it is where the finance forms are explained.

tasks.title: Complete the mandatory finance training module
tasks.detail: Section IIIa — required before you can start the role.

tasks.title: Make the WhatsApp committee chat
Make the CampusTV 2026/27 WhatsApp community and general chat
tasks.detail: Monitor it for bots. Make the whole committee admin.

tasks.title: Add everyone to the Drive as a contributor
tasks.detail: Ela needs manager so she can create marketing folders. Make sure everyone knows to upload edited AND unedited content, plus marketing material.

tasks.title: Order merch — joint order with the other media groups
tasks.detail: T-shirts, hoodies, leaflets. Three to four weeks ahead. A joint order cuts the delivery cost.

tasks.title: Book the freshers fair table
tasks.detail: The booking email lands in the ctvmanager inbox — watch for it.

tasks.title: Book the sports fair table
tasks.detail: Section Ib is emphatic about being at this one: it is where livestreaming gets sold.

tasks.title: Make the QR codes and test them on two phones
tasks.detail: Three of them: the general group chat, the SU page to buy membership, and Instagram. Use a free generator. Test on two phones in case one fails.

tasks.title: Plan the stall: sweets and TV trivia
tasks.detail: Easy / medium / hard questions for 1 / 2 / 3 sweets. Keep the categories on a TV theme — the Office, Gossip Girl, Doctor Who — so it does not overlap with Filmsoc.

tasks.title: Speak to Backstage about the freshers rig
tasks.detail: Note down every item you let them set up so no cable leaves with them. Cameras get rigged with you present.

tasks.title: Sort press access and AAA for the whole team
Check there are enough SD cards
tasks.detail: One goes into the ATEM every arena night and gets emptied at 02:00.

tasks.title: Give the team basic camera and mic training
tasks.detail: Enough that they can go out and do interviews without you.

tasks.title: Get everyone learning DaVinci and sending you what they make
tasks.detail: It is free. The more of them who can edit, the more of pre- and post-production you can hand over when you are busy.

tasks.title: Delegate freshers coverage — who does what, and when
tasks.detail: You need to know when everyone is back in Bath and moved in. Caela used ClickUp for this.

tasks.title: Put up the meet-the-committee post
tasks.detail: The week before freshers.

tasks.title: Make sure the social sec advertises all the groups equally
tasks.detail: Not just URB. If they will not, get Ela to make CTV adverts herself — she will need to be in contact with them either way.

tasks.title: Check the SU what's-on page and decide what to cover in daytime freshers
tasks.detail: Decide as a team. Do not over-commit — most of the team cannot edit yet and the arena night edits still have to happen alongside.

tasks.title: Agree with Joe Rumford which daytime events he is filming
tasks.detail: So you are not both filming the same thing and posting reels about it. He generally covers what he thinks you will miss.

tasks.title: Set up the free Buffer account
tasks.detail: Posts to Instagram, Facebook, YouTube shorts and TikTok at once. You and Ela both need to be logged in and comfortable using it before freshers.

tasks.title: Write the interview questions
tasks.detail: Nothing that insults the SU, promotes drugs or anything illegal. Lighthearted and fun. New questions for arena nights so it does not look like the same two people.

tasks.title: Get 2–3 of the team confident enough to teach
tasks.detail: They need to be able to assist at training and answer questions, not just attend.

tasks.title: Schedule an SU takeover around a big event
tasks.detail: Rugby at the Rec, fight night or a livestream. It is their stories, so plan what you show.

tasks.title: Make a WhatsApp group chat for each event
Put the kit check-in / check-out system in place
tasks.detail: Head of Tech owns it. You need to know what is booked out, when it leaves and when it comes back. Ask Peter — he has thoughts on this.

tasks.title: Find the finance forms and read Caela's examples
tasks.detail: thesubath.com/finance/interactive_forms — and her old emails show what a filled-in one looks like. Ask Helen if you cannot find a finance code.

tasks.title: Learn the new finance system yourself
tasks.detail: It is changing. Do not rely on the treasurer to know how much money you have left — they are often not on top of it.

tasks.title: Set up a way to check SU memberships before anyone touches kit
tasks.detail: SU website → settings → media exec → memberships, cross-checked against the name list.

tasks.title: Ask Chris Lyons about the equipment borrowing scheme
tasks.detail: He and Jade ran it — it let members rent kit safely for their own projects.

tasks.title: Get the alumni fund dates from Helen and Angus
tasks.detail: One window around October/November, one in January. The later you apply the later the money arrives. Read Peter's previous applications first.

tasks.title: Learn the claims flow well enough to teach it
tasks.detail: The finance app is changing. You can claim back some or all of your NaSTA ticket, and you need to be able to show everyone else how.

tasks.title: Agree with the other media groups about sharing kit
tasks.detail: Ours came out of our budget — they should ask, and vice versa.

tasks.title: Update the linktree
tasks.detail: Website, group chats, membership. Effective immediately once the new chats exist.

tasks.title: Set up custom reel covers so the feed reads as one thing
tasks.detail: Short form on Instagram, and use it to push people to YouTube for livestreams and long form.

tasks.title: Update the CampusTV page on the SU website
tasks.detail: Speak to Will Kitchen about how to edit it. This is how a lot of freshers find us, and the linktree points at it.

tasks.title: Speak to Peter about the CTV website
tasks.detail: He owns the domain now.

tasks.title: Get livestreams and long-form onto YouTube
tasks.detail: Treat YouTube shorts like Instagram reels — post the same content to build the channel.

tasks.title: Write down who handles what
tasks.detail: Committee roles and per-event roles. This is the thing that prevents fallouts. Remember it is a society, not a job — adjust responsibility when interest wanes.

tasks.title: Complete the safeguarding training
tasks.detail: You are the HR if it is needed.

tasks.title: Make sure the team know to tell you if something is off
tasks.detail: Especially the women in leadership roles, and especially around Backstage. Caela was explicit about this.

tasks.title: Decide whether to run CTV-only socials
tasks.detail: Someone can take on a CTV social sec role alongside their main one if the group wants it.

tasks.title: Join the NaSTA regional and main group chats
tasks.detail: Caela cannot add you — message the NaSTA Instagram account for the links. The whole team can join everything except the station manager chat.

tasks.title: Read the categories and plan projects to the spec
tasks.detail: nasta.tv/awards, and there is a detailed PDF at the bottom of the page. Plan content to fit categories rather than hunting for entries in April.

tasks.title: Pay the NaSTA membership fee
tasks.detail: The email lands in the ctvmanager account. If the payment gives trouble, message the NaSTA Instagram or ask Helen.

tasks.title: Check every submission against the export settings
tasks.detail: Getting this wrong costs you awards and can invalidate the entry. The settings are in the PDF; ask the NaSTA team if anything is unclear.

tasks.title: Submit for as many categories as possible
tasks.detail: It is the only lever you have on the odds.

tasks.title: Advertise the awards hard, early
tasks.detail: It genuinely is not fun when nobody goes. Push it to everyone who was involved and to the wider media membership. Nominations come out beforehand, but there are unannounced categories — do not let a quiet nominations list put people off.

tasks.title: Book group travel and a shared Airbnb
tasks.detail: Everyone together so you can look after each other. Count the number leaving and the number coming back — people wander off when there is alcohol.

tasks.title: Ask the exec what can be subsidised
tasks.detail: Tickets certainly, accommodation possibly — Helen will know whether the budget can cover it.

tasks.title: Secure a station manager for next year
tasks.detail: Caela's closing note names this as the priority that keeps CampusTV alive. Start looking long before you need to.

tasks.title: Write next year's handover
tasks.detail: CTV OS can export it from everything logged during the year, but it still needs your judgement on top.

tasks.title: Chase Peter for his section of the handover
tasks.detail: Section VIII is still 'TBC when he has time'. He has run the station three times and has the kit check-in/check-out system in his head.

committee.desc: Oversees event organisation, kit purchase, liaising with societies, team management, NaSTA submissions and award attendance.
Runs events with the station manager, or alone if they are unavailable. Organises the role call for events and sorts the team on the day's roles. Can lead project and content-strategy meetings.
Kit hire, kit logs and what gets booked out, risk-assessment forms for events, and maintenance of kit in general — keeping everything in its right place.
Handles socials, promotion of our work and events, and the society in general.
Handles sports events and comms with the groups — building relationships to get us into more sports, and staying aware of events we can cover.

crew.title: Producer
crew.desc: Runs the event on the day with or for the station manager: role call, making sure everyone knows their job, the kit is set, and the coverage plan actually happens.

crew.title: Camera operator
crew.desc: Operates a camera — gantry (roof), SU box or roaming at the Rec, and interviews on welcome/arena nights. Bring the right lens and SD cards, get plenty of B-roll for highlights, and check kit back in at the de-rig.

crew.title: Interviewer
crew.desc: Fronts interviews with freshers, players and punters. Lighthearted, SU-safe questions, clips kept under ~3 minutes, working in a pair with a cam op.

crew.title: Vision mixer
crew.desc: Runs the ATEM on live/arena nights to a pre-agreed shot plan. Loads the SD card and presses record every night; works alongside the PTZ op.

crew.title: PTZ operator
crew.desc: Drives the PTZ camera on live nights to the vision mixer's plan. Ask John Lucas / Destin if unsure how the controller works.

crew.title: Audio
crew.desc: Sets up and monitors sound — radio mics for interviews, a room mic for audience audio (e.g. Dance Soc's tap noises). Never take the sound-desk feed unless it has been agreed.

crew.title: Editor
crew.desc: Cuts and delivers footage — interview clips published the next day, arena-night highlight reels. Ideally the interviewer edits their own clips; the station manager reviews every edit for language and SU slander before it posts.

crew.title: Runner
crew.desc: General support on the day: helping load and carry kit to and from the venue, keeping track of gear, and assisting the crew.

crew.title: Stills
crew.desc: Shoots stills and B-roll for montages and socials.
